why: R11's `environment` signal asks whether our kernel declares anything about
a candidate held-out family's subject operators. It cannot be a threshold,
and measuring it is what shows why: `natural-square-root` is a legitimate
standing held-out family and we declare `Nat.sqrt`, `Nat.sqrt_zero` and
`Nat.sqrt_one` (draw 8 compared all four by hand; none is a mirror), while
a `natural-nth-root` candidate picks up 9 hits on the stem `root` whose top
is `Complex.root_of_unity_pow` -- unrelated mathematics sharing a word. No
count separates those. A person reading five names does, in a minute.
So a NEW held-out family whose sweep is non-empty must be reviewed here
before it may be drawn. The review must reproduce the LIVE sweep exactly:
that is what makes it a disclosure rather than a rubber stamp, because a
later declaration landing in that namespace changes the sweep and
invalidates the review instead of passing silently.
The DEMAND is scoped to draw time. Every standing held-out family was
preregistered before this screen existed, so demanding a review for one
retroactively would mean either a red gate on `main` or a file asserting
diligence nobody performed -- and the second is the checker-that-cannot-fail
defect wearing a paper trail. A STALE review is refused wherever it is
found, because that is a claim someone made.
how_to_add_a_row: R11 prints) to get the live sweep for the family: a list of
2. Read the declarations that sweep names and compare them against the ten
statements the family would draw. You are answering one question: does
our development already settle any of them, under any name?
3. Record the sweep VERBATIM in `swept`, what you found in `finding`, and
the ADR that carries the decision in `authority`. If you found a mirror,
do not write a row -- the family is not blind and must not be drawn.

natural-nth-root.finding: All 11 declarations matching these three stems read by name: CReal.ivt_exact_root, CReal.ivt_exact_root_at, CReal.ivt_exact_root_decides_sign (bisection root-finding over CReal, unrelated construction over a different carrier); Complex.I_is_fourth_root, Complex.IsRootOfUnity, Complex.geom_sum_eq_zero_of_root_of_unity, Complex.one_is_root_of_unity, Complex.root_of_unity_mul, Complex.root_of_unity_pow (roots of unity over Complex, unrelated mathematics sharing the word "root"); Nat.nth, Nat.nthAux (the well-founded selector from draw 7's natural-nth-selector family, a different function despite the shared stem "nth"); and Nat.nthRoot, Nat.nthRootAux themselves (this draw's own ADR-0910 construction, necessarily self-matching). None of the drawn ten statements (Nat.exists_pow_eq_iff, Nat.exists_pow_eq_iff', Nat.le_nthRoot_iff, Nat.lt_pow_nthRoot_add_one, Nat.nthRoot.lt_pow_go_succ_aux, Nat.nthRoot_eq_of_le_of_lt, Nat.nthRoot_lt_iff, Nat.nthRoot_one_right, Nat.nthRoot_pow, Nat.nthRoot_zero_left) is a mirror of any declaration this sweep names -- the kernel has never proved a theorem ABOUT Nat.nthRoot, only the construction itself. Same pattern as the natural-square-root precedent (draw 8): the subject exists, no row is settled.

natural-bit-decode.finding: The "bit" stem's 45 hits are overwhelmingly this kernel's exhaustively-developed native Nat.bit/Nat.bitwise/Nat.testBit family (Nat.bit, Nat.bit_true, Nat.bit_false, Nat.bitwise, Nat.bitwiseAux, Nat.bitwise_and_eq_land, Nat.land_bit, Nat.lor_bit, Nat.ldiff_bit, Nat.testBit and its lemmas, etc.) plus one false positive (CReal.integralSplitArbitrary -- "bit" is a substring of "Arbitrary", unrelated subject, the same false-positive class ADR-0900 already named). The "size" stem's 6 hits are 5 genuine Nat.size declarations (Nat.size, Nat.sizeAux, Nat.size_zero, Nat.size_aux_lt_pow, Nat.lt_pow_size) plus one false positive (CReal.meshLevelCount_ge_of_size, an unrelated CReal integration-mesh construction). Compared against the drawn ten (Nat.bit_add, Nat.bit_add', Nat.bit_false_zero, Nat.bit_le, Nat.bit_lt_bit, Nat.bit_ne_zero, Nat.size_bit, Nat.size_eq_zero, Nat.size_le_size, Nat.size_one): none is a mirror by name, and Mathlib's Nat.bit : Bool -> Nat -> Nat matches our kernel's own Nat.bit signature exactly, so this is a genuine subject-level overlap (this kernel could plausibly prove several of these rows from existing infrastructure) -- the same judgment call ADR-0900 recorded and left unresolved ("a judgement call, and it does not by itself solve this draw"), and the same shape as the accepted natural-square-root precedent (Nat.sqrt/sqrt_zero/sqrt_one already declared, none a literal mirror of the held-out rows). Accepted on that precedent: no row is SETTLED by an existing declaration, only the general subject is developed.
